geometry.locator: arXiv:2407.11912, 'positioned at (20.7 +/- 0.1) m from the reactor core center'
geometry.note: CONUS+'s own paper (arXiv:2407.11912) states the detector sits (20.7 +/- 0.1) m from the reactor core center, 12.45 m horizontal distance from the reactor central axis, inside room ZA28R027 of the KKL containment, i.e. inside the reactor building itself. No fetched source gives the azimuth of that horizontal offset, so this point is the centre of a circle fitted to the circular part of the reactor-building outline (geometry:leibstadt-core, radius 23.0 m), taken as the reactor axis, and the detector lies within 12.45 m of it in an unknown direction. accuracy_m 30 m covers that 12.45 m offset plus the ~10 m uncertainty of the fitted axis.

notes: The point is derived from the OpenStreetMap reactor-building footprint, so it carries the ODbL-1.0 licence.

summary.plain: The approximate position of the CONUS+ coherent-neutrino-scattering detector, which sits inside the Leibstadt reactor building about 20.7 m from the reactor core, since late 2023.
